citations.label: AGMAI, Responsible Release of AI-Generated Mathematics (the problem)
citations.excerpt: However, it is now the case that AI can output mathematical arguments in situations without the human who prompted it being able to understand the arguments, verify them, or take responsibility for them.

citations.label: AGMAI, Responsible Release of AI-Generated Mathematics (exposition)
citations.excerpt: They should not be full of wordy reasoning and non-standard terminology that renders them virtually incomprehensible.

citations.label: AGMAI, Responsible Release of AI-Generated Mathematics (failed attempts)
citations.excerpt: If many results are released at once, then in addition to the results themselves a further document should be written and made public that references all of the released results and explains how many other problems of comparable difficulty the models tried and failed to solve, as well as how the problems were chosen.

citations.label: AGMAI, Responsible Release of AI-Generated Mathematics (formalization status)
citations.excerpt: Where formalization would lead to unacceptable delays, the formalization status of the paper should be clearly stated.

citations.label: AGMAI, Responsible Release of AI-Generated Mathematics (process disclosure)
citations.excerpt: For each result released, the AI lab should make public the name of the model, the prompts used, a (summarized) chain of thought, the time taken, and the estimated cost of computation.

citations.label: AGMAI, statement on OpenAI's release of mathematical results
citations.excerpt: This release is the beginning, not the completion, of the process of human understanding and the incorporation of the work into mathematical knowledge.

citations.label: AGMAI, statement on OpenAI's release (assessment left to the community)
citations.excerpt: While we consider these discussions constructive, it is ultimately up to the mathematical community to assess the extent to which our recommendations were followed successfully, and whether there are others we should suggest.

citations.label: AGMAI, About (funding and affiliation)

citations.label: AGMAI, About (origin of the group)

citations.label: New Scientist, OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof (the claim)
citations.excerpt: OpenAI appears to have made a subtle error when publishing its proofs of the Navier-Stokes problem, a team of mathematicians has claimed.

citations.label: New Scientist, OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof (scope of the claim)
citations.excerpt: The error doesn't mean that the proofs are incorrect or that OpenAI hasn't correctly solved the problem, but it does call into question whether mathematical results generated by AI models can always be relied on.

citations.label: New Scientist, OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof (natural-language bound)
citations.excerpt: In the natural-language proof, an equation in this part requires that a certain value be below m + 4, where m is a whole number.

citations.label: New Scientist, OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof (Lean bound)
citations.excerpt: In the Lean proof, the equivalent value is required to be below m + 5, which is mathematically weaker.

citations.label: New Scientist, OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof (mechanism)
citations.excerpt: If, in the process of auto-formalisation, the AI finds a section of the proof that doesn't compile, it will attempt to find a workaround even if it means diverging from the proof as written in natural language.

citations.label: New Scientist, OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof (time to find it)
citations.excerpt: In all, it took the team about two weeks to identify a true discrepancy, compared with the 88 hours OpenAI said its agents spent generating the proofs.

citations.label: New Scientist, OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof (reader burden)
citations.excerpt: What has to be done with all of these large language model-generated proofs is that they will have to be read by humans, and this creates an enormous extra burden on mathematicians

citations.label: New Scientist, OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof (method)
citations.excerpt: Finding the divergence involved a slightly surreal process of asking ChatGPT to look for potential discrepancies between the natural-language and Lean proofs, then checking them by hand.

citations.label: oai-math-revised, guest post on Terence Tao's blog (the hub's aim)
citations.excerpt: https://github.com/mathcommunity/oai-math-revised/ seeks to be an inclusive effort to improve these write-ups

citations.excerpt: Additionally, the writeup for the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function was human edited for readability.

citations.label: OpenAI, openai/math history at a pinned commit (citation updates)

citations.label: New Scientist, OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof (the producer's response)
citations.excerpt: OpenAI told New Scientist that it is aware of the mismatch between the natural-language proof and the Lean code, and that this doesn't mean that either proof is invalid.

citations.label: New Scientist, OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof (formalisation under way)
citations.excerpt: It says it will rectify any errors in the natural-language proof as they are found, and will also continue the process of formalising the 722 maths papers the firm released this week, only some of which are accompanied by Lean proofs, which themselves haven't been checked by hand.

citations.label: New Scientist, OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof (model-pass candidates)
citations.excerpt: Many of the discrepancies suggested by ChatGPT turned out, on inspection, to be consistent after all.

citations.label: New Scientist, OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof (the issue)
citations.excerpt: The issue is that OpenAI presents the two proofs as identical

citations.excerpt: On 8 September, OpenAI announced that it had found a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem, one of the most famous open problems in mathematics.
